{{Quote|Shoran has gone on ahead but don't worry, he left markers so we could find him in this wilderness.|Qui-Gon Jinn, to Chewbacca, on Alaris Prime|audio=ShoranWilderness.flac|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
'''Markers''' were structures used and built across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by multiple races, such as the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. They were made up of two forked pieces of [[Wood/Legends|wood]] with a banner stretched between them. Markers were able to serve different purposes, such as highlighting a particular building in a settlement or showing a path to a certain location. In [[3000 BBY]], the Gungan thief [[Marsune (Gungan)|Marsune]] used markers in his hidden [[Tree/Legends|forest]] [[Marsune's base|base]] around its [[animal nursery]]. At some point between [[39 BBY/Legends|39]] and [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]], markers were used on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]] during its [[Alaris Prime colonial war|colonization]] attempts by both the Wookiees and the Trade Federation. Markers continued to be used by Gungans during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]

==Description==
{{Quote|Ah, do you see it? There's the next marker.|Qui-Gon Jinn, to Chewbacca on Alaris Prime|audio=NextMarker.flac|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
Markers were structures that were built and used for different purposes across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. They were made up of two [[Wood/Legends|wooden]] poles that were held together at their base by a white material and spread diagonally away from each other. A banner was stretched between the poles, with a vertical rectangle in its center that would be [[Color/Legends|colored]] by the owner. The design of markers remained the same for their different builders.<ref name="SW:GB" />

==History==
{{Quote|Chewbacca's father, Attichitcuk, awaits us to the north. I can see one of his markers now.|Qui-Gon Jinn, to Shoran and Chewbacca|audio=HeSeesYou.flac|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
[[File:MarsunesBase-SWGB.png|thumb|right|300px|Markers at Marsune's base]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3000 BBY]],<ref name="EA" /> on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] thief [[Marsune (Gungan)|Marsune]] used markers with blue-colored rectangles on them, in his [[Marsune's gang|gang's]] secret [[Tree/Legends|forest]] [[Marsune's base|base]] near the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Otoh Sancture]]. Four markers were placed around the [[animal nursery]] in the base, which served to highlight its presence. Marsune used the nursery to hold five [[Nerf/Legends|nerfs]], a species of antlered animal that had been traded to him by Otoh Sancture's leader, [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Gallo/Legends|Gallo]] in exchange for four worker [[Glurrg]]s.<ref name="SW:GB" />

Between the years [[39 BBY/Legends|39]] and [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> markers were used during the [[Alaris Prime colonial war|colonization]] attempts on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Alaris Prime/Legends|Alaris Prime]] by both [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Alaris Prime colonists|colonists]] from the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], who had [[Alaris Prime colonization resolution|legal]] authorization to colonize the world from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and the company known as the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] who were trying to illegally take Alaris Prime. The first Wookiee to land on the moon, [[Attichitcuk/Legends|Attichitcuk]], built a small [[Attichitcuk's camp|settlement]] and left several markers with orange-colored rectangles to show the way to the camps' location.<ref name="SW:GB" /> Later, Attichitcuk's nephew<ref name="TT">''[[Tyrant's Test]]'' establishes that [[Shoran]] is [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca's]] cousin, meaning he is [[Attichitcuk/Legends|Attichitcuk's]] nephew.</ref> [[Shoran]] arrived on the moon and did some [[Scout/Legends|scouting]], leaving several markers behind until he stopped when he encountered an obstruction, a [[Power core/Legends|power core]] that had been built by the Trade Federation. Shoran stayed at his position until<ref name="SW:GB" /> his cousin<ref name="TT" /> and Attichitcuk's [[Gender/Legends|son]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] followed the markers to him with the assistance of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]. Once they had met up with each other, Chewbacca and Shoran destroyed the power core at Jinn's suggestion, and then followed the markers Attichitcuk had left until they reached his settlement.<ref name="SW:GB" />

[[File:Chewie_and_Shoran.png|thumb|left|200px|Chewbacca and Shoran followed Attichitcuk's markers on Alaris Prime.]]
Two markers were later used in another [[Unidentified Wookiee base (Attichitcuk's rescue)|settlement]] on Alaris Prime that was led by Chewbacca. The markers were placed at the entrance to the camp and were a gathering point for the Wookiee warriors who went to [[Rescue of Attichitcuk|rescue]] Attichitcuk, who had been shot and nearly killed by a unit of Trade Federation [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] commanded by [[DRN-38]]. Chewbacca led the Wookiees to save his [[Parent/Legends|father]] and defeat the droids who had injured him.<ref name="SW:GB" />

The Trade Federation also used markers in one of their bases. They placed four of them with gray rectangles around their [[Fortress/Legends|fortress]] in a [[Unidentified Trade Federation base|base]] commanded by the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[SRAM-13]]. The base and the fortress were [[Battle for Alaris Prime|destroyed]] by the Wookiees in an attack that drove the Federation off Alaris Prime.<ref name="SW:GB" />

During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Trade Federation forces led by [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] found the Gungan Boss [[Ganne]] hiding next to a marker. A marker with a red banner was placed at the entrance to the hidden Gungan city [[Rellias]]. Two markers with green rectangles were present at the [[Gungan Sacred Place/Legends|Gungan Sacred Place]] when evacuees from the Trade Federation's [[Siege of Otoh Gunga|attack]] on the Gungan capital [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]] arrived there.<ref name="SW:GB" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Now move ahead to the first marker by right clicking on it.|Qui-Gon Jinn, using the markers to teach players how to move their units|audio=ClickFirstMarker.flac|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
[[File:Markers_scenario_editor.png|thumb|right|250px|The eight different colors that can appear on markers]]
Markers were first mentioned in the [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] by [[Steven L. Kent]]<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref>&mdash;released on [[November 7]], [[2001]]<ref name="PrimaDate">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Galactic-Battlegrounds-Official/dp/0761537503|text=Star Wars Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide}}</ref>&mdash;for the [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'',<ref name="SW:GB" /> released on [[November 11]], 2001.<ref name="GBDate">{{GameSpot|url=games/star-wars-galactic-battlegrounds|text=Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds}}</ref> In the first level of the Wookiee tutorial campaign, "Moving and Attacking," markers are used to teach the player how to move their units. In other campaign levels, markers highlight certain buildings that the player has to destroy or send units to. The objectives section in the fourth level of the Trade Federation campaign, "Capturing the Crown," instructs the player to build a [[Neimoidian Throne]] inside a set of markers, but a set of units called flags are used instead. In the scenario editor mode of the game, markers can be placed by the player, with the color of the rectangle in their center depending on the color chosen by the player for their units. The colors can be blue, red, green, yellow, gray, purple, cyan, or orange.<ref name="SW:GB" />
